name: ballerinax/ai.weaviate
description: Weaviate is an open-source vector database that allows you to store data objects and vector embeddings from your favorite ML-models. The Weaviate connector enables seamless interaction with Weaviate instances, supporting complex vector searches and data management.
readme: ## Overview Weaviate is an open-source vector database that allows you to store data objects and vector embeddings from your favorite ML-models. The Weaviate connector enables seamless interaction with Weaviate instances, supporting complex vector searches and data management. ### Key Features - Seamless storage of data objects and vector embeddings - High-performance vector search and semantic search - Support for modular vectorizers and ML-model integration - Efficient management of schemas and classes - Secure communication with authentication support - GraalVM compatible for native image builds ## Set up guide Before using the Ballerina Weaviate vector store module, you need to set up a Weaviate instance and obtain the necessary credentials. ### Step 1: Create a Weaviate account You can create an account for free if you don't already have one. 1. Visit [weaviate.io](https://weaviate.io/) and click **Try Now** to sign up for a free account 2. Complete the registration process and verify your email address if required 3. Log in to your new Weaviate account For more details, refer to the official documentation on [creating a new account](https://docs.weaviate.io/cloud/platform/create-account). ### Step 2: Set up a Weaviate cluster 1. Access the Weaviate Console and click **Create Cluster** to create a new Weaviate instance. 2. Provide the required details (e.g., Cluster name) and preferred configuration options and confirm. 3. Click **Create** and wait for the cluster to be provisioned (this typically takes 2-3 minutes) 4. Once the cluster is ready, locate and copy the REST endpoint URL from your cluster dashboard. You'll use this URL as the `serviceUrl` in your `weaviate:Client` configuration For more details, refer to the official documentation on [creating clusters](https://docs.weaviate.io/cloud/manage-clusters/create). ### Step 3: Generate API credentials 1. In the Weaviate Console, navigate to your cluster dashboard and go to the API Keys section 2. Click **Create API Key** and provide a name for the key and create the API key. 3. Securely save the generated API key, which you'll use as the `token` in your `weaviate:Client` configuration. For more details, refer to the official documentation on [authentication](https://docs.weaviate.io/cloud/manage-clusters/authentication). ## Quick Start ### Step 1: Import the module ```ballerina import ballerina/ai; import ballerinax/ai.weaviate; ``` ### Step 2: Initialize the Weaviate vector store ```ballerina ai:VectorStore vectorStore = check new weaviate:VectorStore( serviceUrl = "add-weaviate-service-url", config = { collectionName: "add-collection-name" }, apiKey = "mock-token" ); ``` ### Step 3: Add vectors ```ballerina ai:Error? result = vectorStore.add( [ { id: "1", embedding: [1.0, 2.0, 3.0], chunk: { 'type: "text", content: "This is a chunk" } } ] ); ``` ## Examples The Ballerina Weaviate vector store module provides practical examples illustrating usage in various scenarios. Explore these [examples](https://github.com/ballerina-platform/module-ballerinax-ai.weaviate/tree/main/examples). 1. [Book recommendation system](https://github.com/ballerina-platform/module-ballerinax-ai.weaviate/tree/main/examples/book-recommendation-system) This example shows how to use Weaviate vector store APIs to implement a book recommendation system that stores book embeddings and queries them to find similar books based on vector similarity and metadata filtering.

typeDefs.name: Configuration
typeDefs.description: Configuration for the Weaviate vector store.

fields.name: collectionName
fields.description: The name of the collection to use

fields.name: chunkFieldName
fields.description: The name of the field to contain the chunk details

fields.name: httpVersion
fields.description: The HTTP version understood by the client

fields.name: timeout
fields.description: The maximum time to wait (in seconds) for a response before closing the connection

fields.name: compression
fields.description: Specifies the way of handling compression (`accept-encoding`) header

fields.name: circuitBreaker
fields.description: Configurations associated with the behaviour of the Circuit Breaker

fields.name: responseLimits
fields.description: Configurations associated with inbound response size limits

fields.name: validation
fields.description: Enables the inbound payload validation functionality which provided by the constraint package. Enabled by default

typeDefs.name: VectorStore
typeDefs.description: Initializes the Weaviate vector store with the given configuration.

functions.name: init
functions.description: Initializes the Weaviate vector store with the given configuration.

parameters.name: serviceUrl
parameters.description: The URL of the Weaviate service

parameters.name: apiKey
parameters.description: The API key for the Weaviate service

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: The configurations containing collection name, topK, and chunk field name

parameters.name: httpConfig
parameters.description: The HTTP configuration for the Weaviate client connection

return.description: An `ai:Error` if the initialization fails, otherwise returns `()`

functions.name: add
functions.description: Adds a list of vector entries to the Weaviate vector store.

parameters.name: entries
parameters.description: The list of vector entries to add

return.description: An `ai:Error` if the addition fails, otherwise returns `()`

functions.name: delete
functions.description: Deletes a vector entry from the Weaviate vector store.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: One or more identifiers of the vector entries to delete

return.description: An `ai:Error` if the deletion fails, otherwise returns `()`

functions.name: query
functions.description: Queries the Weaviate vector store for vector entries.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: The query containing the embedding, filters, and other search parameters

return.description: A list of `ai:VectorMatch` objects if the query is successful, otherwise returns an `ai:Error`
